correctness.rationale: For each Gaussian objective, its top two additive-grid entries are either the best/second row at the best column, or best row at the best/second column. Both classes are genuine exposed lineup vertices. Independent uniform factor rank permutations yield exact per-vertex probabilities. The normal gap survivor and density are derived by conditioning on the top Gaussian; the collision formula is the sum of squared cone masses. Standard Mills-ratio/Poisson exceedance estimates prove the joint Gaussian spacing limits. The deterministic top-r grid truncation to the first r rows and columns makes the Poisson outer-sum limit a finite continuous-mapping argument. Collision inversion follows from the exact ratio and p/q asymptotics. The included verifier checks all small-orbit witnesses, 13,230 top-r grid tests, quadrature symmetry and seeded simulations, all replayed successfully. These finite checks are not used as proofs of infinite statements.

value.rationale: This is a complete Euclidean angular sampling law for a named convex-polytope family directly motivated by a quantum-marginal lineup construction, not a free Gaussian identity. It identifies a counterintuitive mathematically sharp inversion: the orbit that dominates single exposures becomes negligible among coincident exposures for unequal polynomial factor growth. It gives finite exact collision laws with two solid-angle levels and a coherent fixed-length extreme-lineup Poisson model, enabling quantitative normal-cone sampling beyond known vertex/facet counts and circumsphere data. This is motivated geometric probability rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
